beats.text: The machine was a man in a box.
beats.note: Kempelen would open the cabinet, show the clockwork, wind the key. The clockwork was a decoy. A chess master sat behind it on a sliding seat, working the arm with levers.

beats.name: Wolfgang von Kempelen
beats.role: Built the Turk for the court of Empress Maria Theresa. It beat almost everyone who sat down to play it, and nobody who suspected a hidden operator could prove how it was done.

beats.text: It beat Franklin. It beat Napoleon.
beats.note: Benjamin Franklin in Paris. Napoleon in Vienna, 1809, who tried illegal moves; the Turk shook its head and put the piece back, then won the game.

beats.text: It ran for over eighty years.
beats.note: Kempelen died in 1804 and new owners kept it touring. Edgar Allan Poe watched it and wrote that a mind, not a mechanism, was moving the pieces. Fire took it in 1854.

beats.text: In 2005 Amazon revived the name for humans hidden inside software: "artificial artificial intelligence."

beats.line: The oldest trick in artificial intelligence is a person behind the curtain.
